name: Visual City
description:
A city speaks in images all the time: in the signs, statues, posters, and people we pass without a second glance. Drawing on decades of documenting Bengaluru, this talk explores what its visual culture reveals about the city and its people. How do we look more keenly at the images around us and find their meaning?

Offered by Bengaluru-based multidisciplinary artist Ravikumar Kashi, whose practice spans painting, photography, installation and artist books, the talk explores how close looking can lead to a deeper, more empathetic understanding of the city. A gesture, a fragment, or something left out can matter as much as what is captured.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: A Politics of Friendship—Ambedkar & Gandhi in Conversation
description:
On the eve of Constitution Day, this lecture by Dr. Kanika Gauba, professor at NLSIU, shows why both Gandhi and Ambedkar - particularly, Ambedkar - cannot be limited to their constitutional contributions. Who is a 'friend'? Are they the people we choose, or those who choose us? Do they have to think like us, share our opinions? Are they always 'good' people? In fact, are they always 'people'? Why do we need friends at all?

Philosophers, including the ancient Greeks, have long puzzled over these questions. For all his wisdom, Socrates himself could not define friendship. So the puzzle becomes more complex when we insert politics into the equation. If politics is the pursuit of self-interest, can friendship ever be possible in politics? And if so, what would this 'friendship' mean?

Treating the anticaste intellectual and legal luminary, B.R. Ambedkar, and the anticolonial practitioner of nonviolence, M.K. Gandhi, as men of ideas, this lecture pieces together a radically new form of politics - a politics of friendship. Defying the usual practice of viewing the two as intellectual and political rivals, this lecture dares to put Ambedkar and Gandhi in dialogue with each other.

name: Journey Halfway to the Center of the Earth: how processes deep within the Earth shape the Earth's Surface
description: Separated from the surface by hundreds of kilometers thick blanket of rocks, the Earth’s mantle is invisible to us. However, it is the convective circulation of this “solid” layer of rocks that shapes the surface of the Earth. From the formation of mountains to earthquakes and erupting volcanoes, they owe their occurrence on the processes taking place within this layer. Since direct methods cannot be used to explore this region, geophysicists use indirect ways to understand these processes. Seismic waves generated by earthquakes give some of the clearest pictures of the mantle while gravity measurements also provide important information about this region. In this talk, I will give an overview of some of the research carried out by my group to understand how the processes within the mantle can explain various phenomena occurring on the Earth’s surface. A better understanding of these processes not only helps us understand how this planet has evolved with time, but can also potentially lead to better earthquake forecasting.

name: Book Launch | ‘Mahua Matters’: Stories, Memory and Flavour
description:
Mahua is more than a flower. Rooted in forest ecologies, community knowledge, food cultures and livelihoods, it carries stories that are often overlooked. ***Mahua Matters***, a publication by Wild Harvest India and Edible Issues and *Issue 1* brings together these stories through research, writing and flavour exploration.

Join us for a conversation with editors and the *Mahua Matters* team, **Shivani Unakar** and **Elizabeth Yorke**, contributor **Kumud Dadlani**, and chef **Hanna Sarangan** on the people and places behind the book, followed by a guided tasting that explores mahua’s many flavours and possibilities. Together, we’ll discover what it means to look at this flower in new ways and why its stories matter.

This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience.

name: Side A/Side B: Californication with Sachin Bhatt
description:
A listening session of **Californication, t**he album that gave the Chili Peppers a second life.

The **Red Hot Chili Peppers**' seventh record came out of the band's lowest years and turned into their biggest success. Frusciante came back to the band. The rap-rock novelty label fell away, and what replaced it was Kiedis writing his most reflective lyrics, Flea holding everything up from underneath, and some of the most thoughtful guitar playing at the turn of the century.

The session is hosted by **Sachin Bhatt,** a Bangalore artist who has spent years making visuals for some of music's most loved artists. He's an art director and a vinyl collector, and he makes music in his spare time. On Sunday he brings this record and the story behind his pick.
